questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Nauru?

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter N and has 7 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nauru article.

questions.proof: English and Nauruan are the official languages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Nauru was one of three great phosphate rock (bird droppings) islands in the Pacific Ocean (the others were Banaba (Ocean Island) in _____ and Makatea in French Polynesia).”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter K and has 8 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Nauru article.

questions.proof: Nauru was one of three great phosphate rock (bird droppings) islands in the Pacific Ocean (the others were Banaba (Ocean Island) in Kiribati and Makatea in French Polynesia).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “With 10,670 residents, it is the third least-populated country after Vatican City and _____.”

hints.nudge: It starts with the letter T and has 6 letters.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nauru article.

questions.proof: With 10,670 residents, it is the third least-populated country after Vatican City and Tuvalu.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Nauru is a phosphate rock island, and its main export since _____ has been phosphate.”

hints.nudge: It is a year early in the twentieth century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Nauru article.

questions.proof: Nauru is a phosphate rock island, and its main export since 1907 has been phosphate.
